claim: Open-source river-gauge alarm monitor: 36 alarms on 10 Swiss stations in one real week.
stats: 1 h level forecast error vs persistence (Rhine)
data completeness of one stale station
limit: One calm week only: no official flood level was reached, so real flood detection is untested.
alt: Dark chart of the Muota river discharge over seven days with daily flow pulses above a dashed alarm threshold, red bands marking detected alarm events, and a lower panel showing the rate of rise against its alarm line.
post:
A river does not phone you when its flow jumps. Someone has to watch the numbers, and the data is often late, flat or missing.

I built water-scada-lite, a small open-source monitoring and alarm system for water utilities and small hydropower, and ran it on real open data from the Swiss Federal Office for the Environment: 10 river stations, 5-minute readings, 1 to 8 November 2026.

It flags gaps, flat sensors and spikes, raises threshold and rate-of-rise alarms with hysteresis and acknowledgement, checks a hypothetical small-hydro intake against a minimum flow, forecasts the water level 1 and 3 hours ahead, and publishes to MQTT and a web dashboard.

Measured: 36 alarms in the week, 18 on the Muota, which shows repeated daily flow pulses. One station's feed was 64% complete and stale for over four hours. For the 1 hour forecast, a simple ARX model cut the error from 6.4 cm to 1.4 cm on the Rhine, but it was worse than repeating the last value at 4 of 10 stations.

Not verified: one calm week, no official flood level reached, generic alarm thresholds, assumed residual-flow minima, MQTT tested without a live broker.

Which alarm do you wish your monitoring raised earlier?

Code: https://github.com/VB-Builds/water-scada-lite
